legend: While looking at the kitchen fridge, the little boy Tyler noticed magnets with symbols, that can be aligned into a string s$$$s$$$.

Tyler likes strings, and especially those that are lexicographically smaller than another string, t$$$t$$$. After playing with magnets on the fridge, he is wondering, how many distinct strings can be composed out of letters of string s$$$s$$$ by rearranging them, so that the resulting string is lexicographically smaller than the string t$$$t$$$? Tyler is too young, so he can't answer this question. The alphabet Tyler uses is very large, so for your convenience he has already replaced the same letters in s$$$s$$$ and t$$$t$$$ to the same integers, keeping that different letters have been replaced to different integers.
We call a string x$$$x$$$ lexicographically smaller than a string y$$$y$$$ if one of the followings conditions is fulfilled:

There exists such position of symbol m$$$m$$$ that is presented in both strings, so that before m$$$m$$$-th symbol the strings are equal, and the m$$$m$$$-th symbol of string x$$$x$$$ is smaller than m$$$m$$$-th symbol of string y$$$y$$$.
String x$$$x$$$ is the prefix of string y$$$y$$$ and x≠y$$$x \neq y$$$.
Because the answer can be too large, print it modulo 998244353$$$998\,244\,353$$$.
input: The first line contains two integers n$$$n$$$ and m$$$m$$$ (1≤n,m≤200000$$$1 \le n, m \le 200\,000$$$) — the lengths of strings s$$$s$$$ and t$$$t$$$ respectively.
The second line contains n$$$n$$$ integers s1,s2,s3,…,sn$$$s_1, s_2, s_3, \ldots, s_n$$$ (1≤si≤200000$$$1 \le s_i \le 200\,000$$$) — letters of the string s$$$s$$$.
The third line contains m$$$m$$$ integers t1,t2,t3,…,tm$$$t_1, t_2, t_3, \ldots, t_m$$$ (1≤ti≤200000$$$1 \le t_i \le 200\,000$$$) — letters of the string t$$$t$$$.
output: Print a single number — the number of strings lexicographically smaller than t$$$t$$$ that can be obtained by rearranging the letters in s$$$s$$$, modulo 998244353$$$998\,244\,353$$$.
note: In the first example, the strings we are interested in are [122]$$$[1\, 2\, 2]$$$ and [212]$$$[2\, 1\, 2]$$$. The string [221]$$$[2\, 2\, 1]$$$ is lexicographically larger than the string [2121]$$$[2\, 1\, 2\, 1]$$$, so we don't count it.
In the second example, all strings count except [4321]$$$[4\, 3\, 2\, 1]$$$, so the answer is 4!−1=23$$$4! - 1 = 23$$$.
In the third example, only the string [1112]$$$[1\, 1\, 1\, 2]$$$ counts.

legend.ai: Tyler 这个小男孩在观察厨房里的冰箱时，注意到了一些带有符号的磁贴，这些磁贴可以排列成字符串 s$$$s$$$。

Tyler 喜欢字符串，尤其喜欢那些字典序小于另一个字符串 t$$$t$$$ 的字符串。在冰箱上摆弄磁贴后，他想知道：通过重新排列字符串 s$$$s$$$ 中的字母，可以组成多少个不同的字符串，使得得到的字符串的字典序小于字符串 t$$$t$$$？Tyler 还太小，无法回答这个问题。Tyler 使用的字母表非常大，因此为了方便起见，他已经将 s$$$s$$$ 和 t$$$t$$$ 中相同的字母替换成了相同的整数，并保证不同的字母被替换成不同的整数。
如果满足以下条件之一，我们称字符串 x$$$x$$$ 的字典序小于字符串 y$$$y$$$：
存在这样一个符号位置 m$$$m$$$，该位置在两个字符串中都存在，使得在第 m$$$m$$$ 个符号之前两个字符串完全相同，并且字符串 x$$$x$$$ 的第 m$$$m$$$ 个符号小于字符串 y$$$y$$$ 的第 m$$$m$$$ 个符号。
字符串 x$$$x$$$ 是字符串 y$$$y$$$ 的前缀，且 x≠y$$$x \neq y$$$。

output.ai: 输出一个整数，即通过重新排列 s$$$s$$$ 中的字符可以得到的、字典序小于 t$$$t$$$ 的字符串数量，对 998244353$$$998\,244\,353$$$ 取模。
